summary.text: Visit a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor to find out whether you have severe disability.

details.heading: What counts as severe disability
details.body: You are likely to be assessed as severely disabled if you are unable to perform at least three Activities of Daily Living. These are bathing, dressing, feeding oneself, using the toilet, moving around and transferring.

steps.name: Visit an assessor
steps.text: Visit a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor to find out whether you have developed severe disability.

items: Visit a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor for an assessment.

example_phrasings: How do I know whether I have developed severe disability?

sources.page_title: How do I know whether I have developed severe disability?

quotes.text: You would need to visit a MOH-accredited severe disability assessor to be assessed whether you are severely disabled.

You are likely to be assessed as severely disabled if you are unable to perform at least three Activities of Daily Living (ADLs). These ADLs are bathing, dressing, feeding oneself, using the toilet, moving around and transferring.
